messages:
sarah: FYI I opened a docs PR for the Optimize toolkit to consolidate batching, caching, and quant profiles into one migration guide. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/492 :wave:

jia: Nice — skimmed it. One quick thing: the SDK snippet still uses client.send_batch(...) which is deprecated. We switched to client.generate_batch in the runtime a couple weeks ago.

mike: Oh yeah, SDK change. We should show both the old and new snippet with a short migration note. People still on 0.9 clients will flip otherwise.

sarah: Good catch. I can add a short section. What do we prefer for the new example? Minimal, like this?

    ```python
    from redwood import Client
    client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
    inputs = ["Summarize: ...", "Summarize: ..."]
    resp = client.generate_batch(inputs, batch_size=8, use_cache=True)
    ```

leo: That looks fine. Add a line about the batching tradeoffs: e.g., batch_size=8 default for low-latency, 16-64 for throughput on dedicated pools. Also note that continuous prefix caching helps seq2seq workloads.

ash: Also there's a broken link on the quant profiles anchor — the anchor id changed after the last docs refactor. I hit it from the PR preview.

docs-bot: docs-ci: preview build completed (staging) — 1 warning, 0 failures. Link-checker flagged: /docs/optimize#quant-profiles -> 404

jia: Thanks docs-bot — can we update the link to /docs/optimize/quantization-profiles (new path)?

mike: Also propose we include a small table (or bullet list) recommending quant profiles by latency sensitivity: 
- low-latency: q4_0_opt or q4_1_lp
- balanced: q8_0_mixed
- max-compression (best-effort): q6_0_turbo

leo: Please don't call them "best" in copy — say "highest compression / potential quality trade-offs". QA will complain if it's prescriptive.

sarah: Good point. I'll reword.

ash: I can push a quick link-fix commit and add the SDK snippet replacement. Want me to open a follow-up PR against your branch?

sarah: If you can push to the branch that'd be perfect — saves CI churn. Branch is docs/opt-toolkit-492.

ash: On it. I'll also add a tiny note under "batching" about safe defaults for hosted vs dedicated: hosted -> batch_size <= 8, dedicated -> up to 64 depending on pool.

jia: Can we include the sample command for the quant profile check? e.g., `redwood-opt analyze --profile q4_0_opt --sample-size 1000` so customers can run evals locally.

mike: Yes include that. Also add a single-line example for enabling prefix caching in the SDK call, like `use_cache=True` (you already have it, nice).

leo: Minor nit: in the migration note mention that function-calling examples weren't touched — we should keep parity.

ash: Pushed link fix + updated snippet to branch, tests passing locally. PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/492/files

docs-bot: docs-ci: preview build succeeded (staging) — 0 warnings.

sarah: Awesome thanks everyone. @jia @mike can you two do a quick review of the wording and the quant recommendations? Hoping to merge after that. :eyes:

jia: Will review in ~2 hours.

mike: I'll take a look after stand.

sarah: Thanks — will watch for approvals and then merge. :tada:
